issue.title: replaceState throws away functions in 0.13

repository.name: immutable-js
repository.description: Immutable persistent data collections for Javascript which increase efficiency and simplicity.

body: @WishCow `this.state` should be a plain object, you're not allowed to put classes in there.

So the wiki page I linked to is incorrect? It would make working with immutable.js (and probably other immutable implementions) a pita, since you would have to pack/unpack the object every time you store/retrieve it.

@WishCow I encountered the same thing in 0.12, storing an immutable-js object on the state directly clobbers it,but simply putting it under an attribute works fine. E.g. `state.foo = myImmutableObject`.

I am experiencing this after upgrading to 0.13 as well. It didn't seem to be a problem in react 0.12. It seems to almost make sense that state could be an immutable object since equality comparison is cheap. I could nest my state object under state (this.state.state? yuck) but it seems like it would create a lot of boilerplate code that I didn't need in 0.12

Yeah this bit me bad... I used an immutable.map as all my state and not a plain object, which worked absolutely great in 0.12 and broke in 0.13. This forces me to add a bunch of useless vanilla objects with a single child prop to hold my immutable map.

issue.title: lrload.React.Component is undefined

repository.name: livereactload
repository.description: Live code editing with Browserify and React

issue.body:
I'm trying to setup livereactload, by following the readme, however, I see this in the firebug console when I make a change to the files:

```
TypeError: lrload.React.Component is undefined
lrload.React.Component.prototype.forceUpdate.call(instance._instance)
```

In the console that is running the watch.sh script I see:

```
LiveReactload: new client connected
745622 bytes written to static/bundle.js (0.22 seconds)
LiveReactload: sending reload request to 1 clients
```

I had to modify the watch.sh script a bit, I added --extension, and -t reactify, is it possible those are causing problems? Here is the full script:

``` bash
{ { node_modules/.bin/watchify static/js/index.jsx --extension=.jsx -v -t reactify -t babelify -t livereactload -o static/bundle.js 1>&2; } 2>&1 \
  | while read result; do
    echo "$result"
    [[ "$result" =~ ^[0-9]+[[:space:]]bytes[[:space:]]written  ]] && node_modules/.bin/livereactload notify
  done
} &

node_modules/.bin/livereactload listen
wait
```

**Edit**
I just tried without the --extension=.jsx, same thing.

issue.title: cannot upgrade to react 0.13

repository.name: react-spa
repository.description: Community site SPA based on ReactJS

issue.body: Bear in mind that upgrading to reactjs 0.13 will break the source code, See https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/3418 for more information.

body: Has there been any movement on this? My project has been on hold since I don't know if I should: a.) stay on React 0.12 where I could use Immutable maps for state. b.) Move all my immutable maps to child of a single-item map. or c.) leave things as they are and this will be supported in the future.

@jeffutter AFAIK this is not going to change. Personally I still don't understand why people want to put third-party objects as state, I don't see what benefit there is. What's wrong with just using `setState`?

@syranide For me there were two main advantages.

1.) My stores already deal in immutable hashes, With react 0.12 I didn't have to bother converting them
2.) Deep comparison for updates is _simple_ with immutable objects. With react 0.12 when you setState with an immutable object, if _any_ of it's contents had changed, it would re-render. If it was the same, it would not. Comparing immutable objects is cheap. Deep comparing hashes is not. There is more upfront cost with the immutable objects, but they are way easier to reason about wether or not they have changed.

If there is definitely no plan to support this then I suppose the best plan of action is to to_js everything and manually deep compare?
